sentences: A city private detective is blind, but he has keenly developed his other senses.
Skilled in self-defense, he pursues his work with the help of his faithful guide dog and assistant.
A retired actress, an old friend, comes seeking advice.
Her headstrong 17-year-old stepdaughter, herself a promising actress, is enamored with her leading man, a much older ladies' man.
The leading man, who once had been the retired actress's lover, has convinced the stepdaughter that the retired actress actually wants him for herself and only has married her father for his money.
The father has invented a secret weapon for the country's war effort.
The stepdaughter arrives at the leading man's apartment and finds him dead, with the retired actress there.
The retired actress insists she'd found him that way, but the stepdaughter concludes that the retired actress has killed him and threatens to call the police unless she leaves the father.
The retired actress then turns to the detective, who goes to the leading man's apartment with the guide dog and the assistant, only to find both the body and the rug under it missing.
The detective picks up a clue and barges into the retired actress's house, pretending to be her curmudgeonly "uncle".
The butler is second in command of a German espionage ring, waiting for an opportunity to get the plans for the father's secret weapon.
The butler had one of his henchmen kill the leading man, whose affection for the stepdaughter was beginning to limit his effectiveness.
The spies' ringleader is the stepdaughter's dramatic coach, who spends the night at the family home and immediately suspects the detective is not what he seems.
The father arrives home and the dramatic coach threatens to have the retired actress's face disfigured in the father's presence unless he surrenders the final step to his invention.
The detective, under guard, is locked in the cellar and sends the guide dog for help.
When the butler is sent to kill him, the detective knocks out the light there to gain an advantage in the total darkness, then overpowers him.
The assistant and the guide dog return with the police, and the father and the retired actress leave for the capital.
The stepdaughter, however, remains cheerfully behind to paint the town with her new "uncle."
The sleuth, known by his alias, and his assistant arrive at dockside to meet a Latin American cruise ship.
On board is the sleuth's brother, who is pronounced dead, a victim of suicide, by the homicide inspector.
The brother's shipboard companion offers sympathy but the sleuth has the assistant tail her, as he already knew that the body in the cabin was not his brother.
Tracking the companion to a fashion show at the salon of her employer, the salon owner, the companion is greeted by her fiancé, the fashion editor.
Two other ship passengers, Latin American dancers, the female dancer and the male dancer are there.
A reporter recognizes the sleuth, who follows the companion into her office.
A shot rings out and the companion falls dead.
The sleuth runs into the alley behind the salon and encounters the brother.
The inspector arrives at the scene and arrests the assistant while the sleuth is run down by a speeding car.
The brother takes the unconscious sleuth to his apartment, where the reporter seeks information about the murder.
The assistant is released with a suspended sentence and learns the sleuth will soon recover.
The reporter informs the brother that the murder weapon is missing, prompting the brother to return to the salon owner's salon to investigate.
Seeing the salon owner at a nightclub, the brother informs her that the police have the gun from the murder scene and are tracing its serial number.
The salon owner phones the inspector and gives them the brother's whereabouts.
The brother and the assistant search the salon owner's, where they find the missing gun hidden in a mannequin.
The inspector tracks them down at the salon and when the brother introduces himself, the inspector arrests him for false impersonation, believing the brother is dead.
After proving his identity, the brother is freed and directs the reporter to investigate the fashion editor's photographer.

The brother confronts the salon owner with the gun, forcing her to admit that she hid the weapon to protect her love, the fashion editor who denies murdering the companion and is exonerated by a ballistics expert.
The reporter discovers that the photographer is an illegal alien.
After smoking a cigar, and about to reveal a clue about mass murders to the brother and the assistant, the photographer falls dead, dropping a pile of magazines.

Deducing that the photographer was killed by a poisoned cigar, the same way the suicide victim on the ship was killed, the brother instructs the assistant to pose as the photographer when the male dancer and the female dancer enter his office with guns drawn.
When the brother steps out of the shadows, the pair identify themselves as Mexican counter-espionage agents and explain that the companion was killed because she knew too much.
After the brother notifies the inspector of the photographer's murder, he brings back the photographer's magazines.

Certain that the fashion editor is involved in the murders, the brother and the assistant realize a magazine cover dated December 7, prophesying the naval base attack and another magazine cover indicates an incident will take place that day at an inn on the island.

The brother and the reporter speed off to stop the sabotage, while the sleuth regains consciousness and joins the assistant on a trip to the island where German agents have been preparing for an attack and the fashion editor is one of them.
After capturing the brother and the reporter and locking them in a bell tower, the agents go ahead with their plan to assassinate a Latin American envoy as his aircraft lands.
The brother manages to ring the bell, just as the sleuth steps in front of the diplomat, sacrificing his own life for that of an ally.
With the spy ring smashed, the brother takes up where his brother left off, becoming the new sleuth.
There have been six axe murders in the city.
The police, led by the inspector, have arrested a different man for each crime.
All are impervious to interrogation, and all are diagnosed by the county psychiatrist as being in a state of paranoid schizophrenia.
Walking home late one night, a young woman is about to become the seventh victim when a young man intervenes and scares off her assailant.
The young man, an unemployed actor, escorts the young woman home but fears the attacker will try again.
His vigilance leads to the arrest of the bird shop owner, the proprietor of a bird shop.
The bird shop owner is as uncommunicative as the others.
The police put the young woman in a hotel for the night.
The young man notices the fire axe has been removed from the hallway, and he chases a man down the stairs and outside, but loses him.
The young man believes that the young woman is withholding information that would explain why she is being targeted.
He is certain that behind the murders there is a mastermind whom the young woman somehow knows.
The inspector observes that all of the murderers' surnames begin with B, but he is not interested in hearing about the axeman or in the young man's mastermind theory.
The prisoner, the bird shop owner, reacts oddly when he sees the young woman with the county psychiatrist—he flings a handful of unintelligible scribbled notes at her.
She gives one to the young man as a souvenir, and when he realizes that it is mirror writing, he reads, "Help the bird shop owner the clinic."
To investigate the clinic, the young man gains entry by posing as a psychopath.
He discovers that the murderers have been drawn from a file of discharged incurables, and concludes they were selected by a psychiatrist who incited them to murder.
The young man escapes from the clinic and takes the young woman to a meeting of the psychiatric society.
She does not recognize any of the doctors, but the doctor is absent so they visit his home.
The doctor avoids meeting them by having his assistant take his place, and follows them to the elevated train, where he pushes the young man onto the track before disappearing into the crowd.
The young man survives but requires hospitalization.
The young woman tells him what she has been holding back: she was engaged while living in the foreign city but her fiancé, the missing fiancé, disappeared.
While the young man rests, the young woman is waiting in another room when she sees the missing fiancé walk by.
A nurse insists that it was the doctor, who returned from the foreign city a few months ago.
The young woman follows him, unaware that he has injected the young man with a deadly dose of insulin.
The young man is saved by alert medical staff and telephones the police because he has figured out that the doctor is the mastermind of the murders.
But the director of the clinic was taken in by the young man's performance there and has convinced the police that the young man is a psychopath and responsible for the murders.
The young woman follows the missing fiancé to his house.
He reveals that he is impersonating his former employer, the doctor, in order to steal the fortune that the man inherited shortly before dying in the foreign city.
The doctor worked on the continent for thirty years and nobody in the city knows what he looked like.
The six axe murder victims were people who knew the missing fiancé in the foreign city.
The young woman is the last person in the city who can identify the missing fiancé as an impostor.
The young woman tries to escape but the missing fiancé knocks her out and hides her in a closet as the police arrive, looking for the young man.
Believing him to be a homicidal maniac, they arrest the young man when he shows up, and ignore his accusations against the doctor.
But when the county psychiatrist notices one of the bird shop owner's notes—that could only have been left by the young woman—he wants to search the house.
The missing fiancé/the doctor panics and tries to flee but is shot dead.
The young man finds the young woman and they intend to get married immediately.
A convicted murderer, the convict (an actor), escapes from police custody, crashing through a washroom window as a train pulls into the main railway terminal in the city.
He telephones his former girlfriend, the stage star (an actress), and threatens to kill her.
She leaves her show between acts and hides in a private train car on a siding at the terminal, planning to leave town and marry her rich, high society fiancé.
The fiancé (an actor).
However, her body is found by the fiancé and his ex-fiancée (an actress).
The police inspector (an actor) is called in to solve the crime.
The doctor at the scene is unable to determine the cause of death.
The convict is recaptured, and the wisecracking private detective (an actor), whom the convict had hired, is also brought in, as he had helped his client evade the police.
Other suspects are rounded up: the stage star's greedy phony psychic stepfather (an actor); her ex-husband (an actor), who works at the terminal; and her producer (an actor).
Also mixed in are the stage star's maid, an ex-burlesque singer (an actress) and her daughter (an actress), the stage star's understudy.
Then the chairman (an
actor), the ex-fiancée's wealthy and influential father—chairman of the board of the railroad—shows up to guard his daughter's interests.
The inspector gets each to tell what they know, with the unwelcome assistance of the private detective.
It turns out that the victim was a calculating gold digger.
Like the inspiration of her stage name, the legendary king, everything (or rather every man) she touched, turned to gold for her purse.
She had used each successive boyfriend as a stepping stone, then discarded each in turn, in her climb up the social ladder.
Landing the millionaire fiancé was to have been her crowning achievement, the fulfillment of her lifelong ambition.

The producer finds her, but she calms his anger at the prospect of losing the star of his expensive production by telling him that she plans to get a rich divorce settlement in about six months, more than enough to finance an even more lavish show.
This conversation is overheard by the fiancé, giving him a motive.
During the investigation, the stepfather dies, apparently of a weak heart.
The private detective is able to solve the case and show that the stepfather too had been murdered.
The killer electrocuted the stage star while she was in the shower of the locked railway car by connecting the plumbing to the electrified third rail.
When he went to return the wiring to the storage locker, he was spotted by the stepfather.
The murderer paid the stepfather off, but later got rid of the loose end with poison.
The private detective identifies the man as the chairman, who breaks away and jumps aboard a departing train, but falls to his own death on the third rail.
When the convict is paroled, he sets out to give $100,000 worth of diamonds to his daughter.
Aware that several shady characters know he has the jewels, he stashes them in a safe deposit box in the office building.
The daughter later receives a call asking her to meet him there, but he never shows up.
She contacts her father's only real friend: a man better known by his nickname.
He agrees to help and drops the daughter off at the apartment of his wealthy friend for safekeeping.
His sidekick has to postpone his wedding to the statuesque bubble dancer.
The father's friend discovers which deposit box the convict rented.
Meanwhile, three crooks, the first crook, the second crook and the third crook, force their prisoner, the convict, to reveal where he hid the diamonds.
When the trio leave, the convict manages to telephones the police, but is killed by the first crook.
The inspector learns enough from the call to rush over to the office building with the sergeant.
He apprehends the father's friend on suspicion of murdering the convict just as he is about to open the box.
The box turns out to be empty.
The father's friend manages to escape.
When he returns to the wealthy friend's apartment, he finds that the daughter has been kidnapped.
A note offers to exchange her for the diamonds.
The father's friend has the sidekick "borrow" a brooch from the bubble dancer, and pries off the fake diamonds.
He then heads to the nightclub, run by the first crook and his associates.
Slipping inside undetected, he spies through the keyhole of the door to the first crook's office and sees the crook put the diamonds in his safe.
After the first crook leaves, the father's friend enters, cracks the safe and takes the jewels.
However, before he can leave, the second crook and the third crook enter.
Thinking quickly, the father's friend drops the diamonds in a pitcher of water.
Unaware that the first crook double crossed them and had the real diamonds, the second crook and the third crook exchange the daughter for the fakes.
The first crook returns too soon and exposes the fakes, but the father's friend and the daughter eventually manage to escape, aided by a citywide wartime practice blackout.
The second crook figures out that the first crook is out for himself.
When he cannot produce the diamonds, the first crook is shot and killed by the second crook.
The father's friend returns to retrieve the stones, and witnesses the murder.
Afterward, he offers to give the jewels to the second crook for the location of the convict's body.
When the police close in, the pair sneak out and steal the inspector's car.
The father's friend sets the radio to "send" without the second crook noticing, then gets him to confess all with the police listening in.
Eventually, the father's friend is able to turn the tables and turn the second crook over to the authorities.
The sidekick's wedding is interrupted once more, this time by the inspector and the sergeant when they arrest the bubble dancer for bigamy.
In 1942, the German state attempts to bring the neutral Turkish state into the war on its side by staging an assassination attempt on its ambassador to the country.

Much to the annoyance of the colonel (an actor), the ambassador survives and the Russians that his agent provocateur was trying to frame have solid alibis, forcing him to turn to another scheme to inflame the Turkish state's traditional rivalry with the Russian state.
An American machinery salesman, the salesman, (an actor) boards the international express train at a city on the line and is attracted to another passenger, the woman passenger (an actress).
Worried about being searched by customs agents once they reach the Turkish border, she asks the salesman to hold on to an envelope containing some securities, all that remains of her inheritance.
The salesman obliges but when he later examines the envelope, he finds maps of the Turkish state with handwritten annotations on them.
When they stop in the capital, he goes to her hotel to return her property, only to find she has been fatally wounded.
He hides when someone else approaches the room.
He watches unobserved as the Soviet spy (an actor) searches the dead woman's luggage.
Then, the salesman exits through the window.
Leaving the scene, he is seen by a woman (an actress), the Soviet spy's sister and partner in espionage.
Turkish policemen take the salesman in for questioning but they are German agents.
They take him to their leader, the colonel, who wants the maps.
The salesman refuses to cooperate and is taken away to be interrogated by the interrogator (an actor).
Before the Germans get very far, the salesman is rescued by the Soviet spy.
When the brother and sister reveal that they are Soviet agents, the salesman agrees to fetch them the documents.
Unfortunately, he finds his hotel room has been ransacked and the documents stolen.
The salesman, it turns out, is also a spy (for his own country).
When he reports to his boss (an actor), he is assigned an assistant (an actor).
The two men head to the largest city.
There, the colonel has bribed a newspaper publisher to print an article claiming that the documents are secret Russian plans for the invasion of the Turkish state.
When the salesman barges in by himself, he is quickly taken prisoner.
The brother and sister have also been captured.
The salesman and the spy's sister get away, but the Soviet spy is killed during the escape.
The salesman kidnaps a German embassy official and learns where the colonel has gone.
The salesman heads to the newspaper, where he forces the German ringleader at gunpoint to burn the maps.
The colonel is handed over to the Turkish police and then to his greatly displeased superior.
He departs by airplane, knowing he is doomed for his failure.
The salesman and the spy's sister head to another foreign capital for their next assignments.
During the Great Depression, a man is ejected from a speeding car.
When he regains consciousness in a hospital, he has amnesia.
He is visited by a man who accuses him of faking his condition.
The stranger calls the patient by a first name and demands to know what happened to a valise, then flees when the patient summons a nurse for help.
When the man recovers, he assumes a new name after a hospital benefactor.
The amnesiac's doctor wants to continue treating him and allows the amnesiac to live at his house.
When all attempts to discover the amnesiac's identity fail, he begins to research his condition.
After ten years, he has become a successful psychiatrist, in partnership with the doctor.
The amnesiac begins treating prison inmates.
He is so successful that he is named head of the state parole board.
While on a date in a nightclub with a social worker, the amnesiac is recognized by two men from his past, the first crook and the second crook.
Along with a third man, the third crook, the men are unsure if the amnesiac is their partner in crime.
They convince a woman convict, their associate's ex-girlfriend, to apply for parole.
At her hearing, she calls the amnesiac by a different surname.
The amnesiac badgers her until she reveals that he is the man of that name, the mastermind of a $200,000 payroll robbery from which the money was never recovered.
To trigger his memory, he contacts the three men and reenacts the events of the day on which he lost his memory.
Tempers flare and the men fight, and during the struggle, the amnesiac is struck on the head, triggering memories of his past.
With the men at gunpoint, he calls the police and has them arrested.
The amnesiac insists on a trial for the robbery.
He admits his wrongdoing but takes pride in his accomplishments since the crime.
The jury finds him guilty but recommends clemency.
The judge sentences him to the minimum term of ten years but suspends the sentence, saying, "We need men like you."
A student at the girls' seminary asks the sleuth, also known by his alias, for his help to investigate a death predicted by her unstable roommate, a clairvoyant.
The professor has recently died, with uncertainty as to whether it was suicide or homicide.
The sleuth gets a ride from town to the seminary with the three daughters of the caretaker, known by a shared nickname, by the school driver.
Posing as an insurance investigator, the sleuth meets the dean, the school's psychology teacher, the drama teacher and the music teacher.
The inspector and the detective are also looking at the local coroner's verdict of suicide.

The sleuth begins his investigation in the professor's room and then goes to the undertaker's, where he finds out it is assumed the professor committed suicide by taking an overdose of sleeping pills.

Believing the death was murder, a group of suspects are carefully watched by the sleuth, including the roommate, who thinks she has inherited her father's insanity, and a love triangle involving the psychology teacher, the music teacher and the drama teacher, all with motives for murder.

Before the sleuth can confront the killer, the dean is murdered and when the roommate tells the music teacher that she saw her standing over the dead body of the dean, the music teacher tries to force the hysterical roommate to jump from the cliffs by the school.
The sleuth races to the cliffs and startles the music teacher, who topples to her death.

She had been behind all the murders, starting with the professor who was killed in a jealous rage and the dean, who would have dismissed the psychology teacher, whom the music teacher had married in secret, as married couples could not work at the school.
Later, the student's mother, a famous actress, arrives at the school with another actress who asks the sleuth to solve a murder at the theater.
At a city airport, a passenger plane coming in from the capital, crash-lands, however nobody is on board.

The aircraft had been hijacked at its previous stop and all of the passengers, except the pilot, leading industrialist the tycoon and his assistant the aide, are found stranded at a rest stop; $100,000 worth of securities are also missing.
Although he promised his fiancée from the southern state, the girlfriend, that he will give up solving crime, the sleuth, aka the gentleman detective, can't resist the lure of a fresh mystery.
When the tycoon's daughter the heiress receives a ransom note, she asks for his help in locating her father.
One of the gentleman detective's prime suspects is the heiress's jealous cousin the relative.
The police inspector and his assistant, the junior officer, are called to investigate the mystery.

The heiress is told to leave $25,000 at a drinking fountain, while the relative tells the sleuth that she suspects the heiress's fiancé the young man told the kidnappers about the $100,000 in securities.
The sleuth accompanies the relative and the heiress to the family's house and later sees the heiress leave a box by the drinking fountain.
When two men collect the box, the sleuth follows their car on horseback and finds it belongs to an antique store owned by the dealer.

The police inspector announces that the tycoon has returned home alive; he and the aide stayed on the aircraft but strangers robbed the tycoon at gunpoint and ordered him to parachute from the aircraft while the pilot set the controls on autopilot.
The sleuth also finds a piece of junk that appears to be part of the aircraft and the missing securities, which he turns over to the police inspector.
The police inspector suspects the aide but state troopers report the missing pilot and the aide have been found dead in a field.
The dealer becomes the next likely culprit but disappears.
As he unravels the mystery, the sleuth reconstructs the second part of the flight.
With other passengers gone, the tycoon killed the aide who had proof of the tycoon's cheating the government, then after take-off, had also killed the pilot and dumped the bodies.
The tycoon's dog attacks the dealer in the antique store.
The police inspector arrives in time to see the sleuth shoot and kill the tycoon in self-defense.
Later at the airport, the girlfriend tells the sleuth she is going home to the southern state by herself.
Dejected, the sleuth declares that he is forsaking all women, until a pretty co-ed approaches him asking for his help.
Amateur sleuth the investigator, known as the gentleman detective, is approached by the young woman to help in finding her brother the young man, who had gone missing.
When the investigator goes to a cocktail bar, he is attacked and knocked unconscious.
When he revives, he finds himself in his car on a country road.

A motorcycle police officer stops him and arrests him because the police inspector has put out an "all-points" bulletin for his arrest in the case of a murdered bank official and the theft of $250,000 in war bonds.

Although the gentleman detective has an alibi with his fiancée, reporter the journalist and assistant, the sidekick supporting him, the police inspector is skeptical and attempts to incarcerate the investigator, who makes his escape.
Returning to the bar, it is now the headquarters of a woman's knitting society, run by the society matron.

When the trio of sleuths head off to the society matron's resort hotel, they find a number of suspicious individuals, including hotel manager the manageress, former criminal the racketeer, the attendant, a nurse to invalid the patient and the young woman.
When the investigator approaches the young woman, she pretends that she doesn't know him and dives into the pool but as she hits the water, she is killed by a gunshot.
Looking for the killer, the investigator runs into puppeteer the showman, who alerts the police inspector that the gentleman detective is at the hotel.
Picking up a cigarette case that might be a clue to the murderer, the investigator has to work quickly before the police inspector arrives.
The journalist reports that the fingerprints on the cigarette case belong to a notorious thief known as the aristocrat.
The investigator phones his houseboy the servant, telling him to pose as the Chinese Trade Commissioner wanting to buy war bonds.

After the patient confides to the servant that he plans to buy war bonds from the manageress, the investigator exposes the society matron as the aristocrat and accuses her of stealing the bonds but the police inspector, with a warrant for murder, arrests the investigator, the journalist, the sidekick and the servant instead.
Finding a way to escape once again, the investigator returns to the hotel and confronts the society matron, who was being blackmailed by the racketeer into selling the war bonds.
When the racketeer is killed, a terrified manageress confesses that she was involved because the racketeer was her husband.
When he is trapped in an elevator with the manageress, the investigator realizes that the killer is still in the hotel.
Finding a way out, the investigator rushes to the society matron's room to find the showman threatening her.
When the investigator tries to apprehend him, the showman falls to his death.
The police inspector, now convinced in the investigator's innocence, arrives to arrest the society matron for the theft of the war bonds.
